STEP 1 - Scene: Cooked bacon strips (three or four pieces) on a white plate. This looks like a breakfast side.

STEP 2 - Vessel: A square white plate, roughly 22 cm across. Area ≈ 22 x 22 ≈ 484 cm² (treating it as a square-ish plate; a round equivalent of ~24 cm would give ~452 cm²). I use ~470 cm².

STEP 3 - Items: Cooked bacon (several strips, some crisp and dark, some lighter and fattier). No visible sauce or oil pool.

STEP 4 - Area: Bacon covers roughly 30% of the plate, concentrated in the central and upper-right region. Food total ≈ 30%.

STEP 5 - Volume: Bacon area ≈ 0.30 x 470 ≈ 141 cm². Bacon strips are thin and layered, with a typical pile height of about 0.8 cm. Gross volume ≈ 141 x 0.8 ≈ 113 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Bacon is meat-like, bulk density ~0.9 g/ml. Mass ≈ 113 x 0.9 ≈ 102 g. Given the strips are flat, this is a reasonable estimate; I'll state about 100 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Cooked bacon ≈ 540 kcal/100 g (pan-fried, fat rendered). 100 g x 5.4 ≈ 540 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: Four to five cooked bacon strips weigh roughly 60–100 g and contain about 400–550 kcal, so this is plausible for what's visible. Taking the lower-middle of that range, I estimate about 90 g and about 490 kcal.
